source: User-submitted visualization follow-up and matching widget state

attempt.choice: Give everyone a short demonstration of the app.
attempt.reason_verbatim: actually i dont see how the app really work, thats why i would choose first option, because only 5 min demonstration can help everyone to know how work the app

support.choice_format: Three supplied action options; own free-text reason.
support.before_attempt: Case flow and clickable evidence. Staff know how to read the screen; no one assigned to monitor it.
support.after_attempt: Widget displays conditional consequence for training. Chat feedback follows; not counted as learner answer.

feedback.valid_reasoning: A demonstration can help if the relevant problem is unfamiliarity with the app. Learner gives a purpose for the intervention.
feedback.case_fit: Case states staff already know how to read the screen. Observed responsibility gap remains even after demonstration. Training does not establish who monitors the screen.
feedback.concept: Tool-based perspective: demonstration/training is a practical intervention; select tools against the observed need. Organisational change includes responsibilities and coordination.
feedback.ambiguity: I dont see how the app really work may refer to the learner needing a clearer view of the fictional app, rather than a claim that staff lack skills. Ask before classifying it as misconception.
feedback.interface_limitation: The pilot depicted the order route but did not demonstrate an app interface.
feedback.language: Meaning understandable; no separate grammar correction requested.
feedback.five_minute_limit: Five minutes is the learner’s proposed duration, not validated as sufficient.

pending_clarification: Did the learner mean that the game did not show the app clearly, or that staff needed app instruction?
next_action: Clarify interpretation, show app-order route if needed; then a fresh transfer situation. Do not grade unresolved interface ambiguity as subject error.
